chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha'i that he had heard Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:
There are eight who will carry God’s Throne. Each one of them has eight eyes, each of which equals all this world.

key_terms.طِبَاقُ الدُّنْيَا: Equals the world / Equivalent to the world

ai.seo_question: How many carriers of the Throne are there and what are their characteristics?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this narration highlights the majestic scale of the Throne Bearers, emphasizing their immense perceptual capacity with eight eyes each, where every eye encompasses the entire world. This description underscores the divine power and the vastness of creation, reflecting the Shia tradition's emphasis on the literal yet transcendent nature of celestial beings. The imagery serves to illustrate the grandeur of Allah’s dominion, connecting the physical structure of the universe with spiritual awareness.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 8-4 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Munqeri, on the authority of Hafs ibn Qiyath al-Nakha’ee that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,
“There are eight who will carry God’s Throne. Each one of them has eight eyes each of which equals all this world.”
